concerns.text: T004 (producer of window selection) prescribes 'stratified random window start indices' while T023 later rewrites code/generate_mobius.py to the FR-002-corrected '100 non-overlapping windows per L (contiguous tiling)'. Two tasks targeting the same producer module prescribe contradictory sampling schemes; the downstream consumers T005/T006 are ordered against the superseded T004 output. Reconcile T004's description with T023 (or mark T004's sampling clause as superseded) so the dependency chain has one authoritative producer.

T005 writes demo_autocorr.csv and T006's integration test asserts on the demo pipeline BEFORE T023 updates the demo path to the final FR-002 sampling contract ('Update the demo path in code/main.py --demo to use this sampling so the early end-to-end run exercises the final contract'). As ordered, the verified end-to-end evidence (T006) is produced against the pre-correction sampling and is invalidated by T023's change; T005/T006 should be sequenced after (or re-run as part of) T023.

T000 (checksum of mobius_array.npy) is numbered before T001 but listed after T004, its producer. Dependency-wise the placement is correct, but the ID ordering (T000 appearing fifth) invites mis-execution; renumber or add an explicit 'depends on T004' note. Also note T000 and T022 both write data/checksums/manifest.sha256 — sequential is fine, but T022 should state it appends/merges rather than overwrites T000's entry.
